name: Single-Leg Balance
description: Single-leg balance is a foundational proprioception and balance rehabilitation exercise. Standing on one leg challenges the ankle stabilizers, peroneals, gluteus medius, and the entire proprioceptive chain from foot to hip. It is a standard initial exercise in ankle sprain rehabilitation, ACL reconstruction recovery, and fall prevention programs. Progressions include eyes closed, unstable surfaces, and reaching tasks.

execution.starting_position: Stand tall near a wall or support for safety. Lift one foot slightly off the ground.
execution.setup_instructions: Perform near a wall for safety. Progress to eyes closed or a folded mat for increased difficulty.
steps: Step 1: Stand tall with feet together, holding a fixed object lightly for safety if needed.
Step 2: Lift one foot off the floor, bending the knee to approximately 90 degrees.
Step 3: Balance on the standing leg, keeping the hip level (do not let the lifted-side hip drop).
Step 5: Switch sides. Progress to eyes closed when 30+ seconds with eyes open is easy.
common_mistakes: The stance hip drops toward the lifted side — the gluteus medius must work to prevent this (Trendelenburg sign)
Grabbing the support heavily rather than using it as a safety touch only
Looking at the feet — fix a point at eye level for best balance
safety_considerations: Always stand near a fixed support — balance challenges can result in falls
In acute ankle sprain rehab, begin on a firm surface with eyes open before progressing
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Upright stance, standing knee very slightly bent, stance hip level.
coaching_cues: Find a fixed point at eye level and stare at it
Keep the hip of the standing leg level — do not let it drop
Grip the floor with your toes for extra stability
